references.text: Jesus commands the rich young man to sell all he owns and give it to the poor – the same call to sell possessions and give alms ([ref:Luk 18:22|Luke 18:22]).

The conclusion of the parable of the rich farmer, where Jesus warns against storing up treasures for oneself without being rich toward God – the background for the exhortation in verse 33 ([ref:Luk 12:21|Luke 12:21]).

Jesus says in the Sermon on the Mount that one should not store up treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, but in heaven – a parallel about heavenly treasure and the contrast to earthly decay ([ref:Matt 6:19-20|Matthew 6:19-20]).
Jesus tells the rich young man to sell everything and give to the poor, and he will have treasure in heaven – a parallel in Matthew to the call to sell and give ([ref:Matt 19:21|Matthew 19:21]).

Paul urges the rich to be generous and share with others, so that they store up for themselves a good foundation for the future – the same idea of heavenly treasure through generosity ([ref:1 Tim 6:17-19|1 Timothy 6:17-19]).
The first Christians sold their possessions and distributed to all as anyone had need – a practical fulfillment of Jesus' words to sell what one owns and give alms ([ref:Apg 2:45|Acts 2:45]).
Jesus encourages giving alms from what is inside – a related exhortation about generosity and almsgiving ([ref:Luk 11:41|Luke 11:41]).

Proverbs warns against striving for wealth, for it makes wings and flies away – the transience of earthly riches, in contrast to the inexhaustible treasure in heaven ([ref:Ordsp 23:4-5|Proverbs 23:4-5]).
Isaiah says that moth shall eat them up like a garment – the background for the image of moths destroying earthly property ([ref:Jes 51:8|Isaiah 51:8]).
James says that wealth has rotted and moths have eaten their clothes – the same image of moths and decay threatening earthly riches ([ref:Jak 5:2-3|James 5:2-3]).
Peter speaks of an inheritance in heaven that cannot perish, spoil, or fade – a parallel to the inexhaustible, imperishable treasure in heaven ([ref:1 Pet 1:4|1 Peter 1:4]).
